findings.summary: Bramblewood achieves a higher mean NDCG@10 (41.2%) than Larkspur-Seq (40.7%) on the Brightcart-Grocery test period, but no statistical test is reported, so the difference cannot be claimed as significant or reliable.
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported; difference is in means only.

findings.summary: Bramblewood's mean NDCG@10 (41.2%) is substantially higher than Most-Popular's deterministic NDCG@10 (18.3%) on the same test period.
findings.caveats: Most-Popular is deterministic; no statistical test reported.

findings.summary: Bramblewood also shows higher mean Recall@20 (63.8%) than Larkspur-Seq (63.1%) and Most-Popular (37.9%), but no significance test is reported.

sentences.text: On the Brightcart-Grocery test period, Bramblewood achieved a higher mean NDCG@10 (41.2% ± 0.7%) than Larkspur-Seq (40.7% ± 0.6%), although no statistical test was reported, so this difference cannot be claimed as significant.
Bramblewood's mean NDCG@10 was also substantially higher than the deterministic Most-Popular baseline (18.3%).
Bramblewood similarly showed higher mean Recall@20 (63.8% ± 0.8%) than both Larkspur-Seq (63.1% ± 0.8%) and Most-Popular (37.9%), again without a reported significance test.
